sentences.en: Today, days after the shooting in Parkland, Florida, with students from the school looking on, state lawmakers voted to not even consider gun control.
sentences.zh: 今天，在佛罗里达州帕克兰发生枪击案几天后，在学校学生们的注视下，州议员们投票决定甚至不考虑枪支管制问题。

sentences.en: What changed their minds?
sentences.zh: 是什么改变了他们的想法？

sentences.en: It's Thursday, March 15th.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月15日，星期四。

sentences.en: Patty, can you tell me a little bit about Florida and its relationship to guns?
sentences.zh: 帕蒂，你能跟我聊聊佛罗里达州及其与枪支的关系吗？

sentences.en: Florida is a great state to be a gun owner.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达州对枪支拥有者来说是个好地方。

sentences.en: Patty Mazze is a national reporter for The Times.
sentences.zh: 帕蒂·马泽是《纽约时报》的全国记者。

sentences.en: And it's been a laboratory for years for the National Rifle Association.
sentences.zh: 多年来，它一直是美国全国步枪协会（NRA）的试验场。

sentences.en: We're a gun state.
sentences.zh: 我们是一个拥枪州。

sentences.en: People in Florida love their guns.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达人热爱他们的枪支。

sentences.en: This is a state that invented the concealed carry permit, where all you need to do is pass a very simple protocol and pay a fee to get a permit.
sentences.zh: 这个州发明了隐蔽携带许可证制度，你只需要通过一个非常简单的程序并支付一笔费用，就能获得许可证。

sentences.en: The Florida Gun Show at the Lee Civic Center in North Fort Myers makes it possible for people to get a gun and the permit to carry it.
sentences.zh: 位于北迈尔斯堡李市政中心的佛罗里达枪展，让人们可以轻松买到枪支并获得携带许可证。

sentences.en: The state has more concealed carry permits than any other state in the country by a lot.
sentences.zh: 该州拥有的隐蔽携带许可证数量远超全国其他任何州。

sentences.en: I mean, we're talking more than 1.7 million permits in a state that has 20 million people.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在一个拥有2000万人口的州，我们谈论的是超过170万份许可证。

sentences.en: So almost one in 10 Floridians has a concealed carry permit.
sentences.zh: 所以几乎每10个佛罗里达人中就有一个持有隐蔽携带许可证。

sentences.en: We'll move over to Disney World.
sentences.zh: 我们转到迪士尼世界看看。

sentences.en: Machine Gun America is a new theme park in Orlando, Florida, where kids as young as 13 years old shoot guns, including AK-47s.
sentences.zh: “机枪美国”是佛罗里达州奥兰多市的一个新主题公园，在那里，年仅13岁的孩子就可以射击包括AK-47在内的枪支。

sentences.en: And the state has been so friendly to gun rights that it has been dubbed the gunshine state.
sentences.zh: 而且该州对枪支权利非常友好，以至于被称为“枪支阳光之州”。

sentences.en: And how did the gunshine state actually become the gunshine state?
sentences.zh: 那么，“枪支阳光之州”究竟是如何形成的呢？

sentences.en: Well, the story of how Florida got here can be told through sort of a legendary figure in Tallahassee political circles.
sentences.zh: 嗯，佛罗里达州走到今天这一步的故事，可以通过塔拉哈西政治圈里的一位传奇人物来讲起。

sentences.en: We have a responsibility to youngsters to make sure that they learn the right things about firearMs.
sentences.zh: 我们有责任确保年轻人了解关于枪支的正确知识。

sentences.en: Marion Hammer runs the NRA chapter in Florida.
sentences.zh: 玛丽恩·哈默负责NRA在佛罗里达的分部。

sentences.en: She's the former president of the NRA, the first female president over the organization.
sentences.zh: 她是NRA的前任主席，也是该组织的第一位女性主席。

sentences.en: And if they don't feel passionate about the Second Amendment and freedom and liberty, then they're the generation that could lose it all for this nation.
sentences.zh: 如果他们对第二修正案、自由和解放没有热情，那么他们这一代人可能会让这个国家失去这一切。

sentences.en: She moved to Tallahassee in the late 70s.
sentences.zh: 她在70年代末搬到了塔拉哈西。

sentences.en: And in the late 80s, she was the one who masterminded the concealed carry permit law.
sentences.zh: 在80年代末，正是她策划了隐蔽携带许可证法案。

sentences.en: And since then, most states have adopted some version of this law, but people forget that Florida was firSt.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，大多数州都采用了该法律的某种版本，但人们忘记了佛罗里达是第一个。

sentences.en: And what led to Marion Hammer pushing for the concealed carry law in the first place?
sentences.zh: 那么，当初是什么促使玛丽恩·哈默推动隐蔽携带法案的呢？

sentences.en: Well, one of the guys leaned out of the back window of the car.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其中一个人从车后窗探出身子。

sentences.en: She has said that she was approached by a carload of young men who she thinks were going to try to rob her, to assault her.
sentences.zh: 她说，当时有一车年轻人靠近她，她认为他们是想抢劫她、袭击她。

sentences.en: I stepped behind a big column and reached in my purse and pulled out my gun.
sentences.zh: 我躲到一根大柱子后面，伸手进包里掏出了枪。

sentences.en: And I stepped out and I drew the gun up through the headlights of the car and I aimed at the driver.
sentences.zh: 我走出来，把枪举过车灯，瞄准了司机。

sentences.en: And she had a handgun and was able to scare them away.
sentences.zh: 她当时带着一把手枪，成功把他们吓跑了。

sentences.en: And so she always makes an argument for self-defense.
sentences.zh: 所以她总是为自卫辩护。

sentences.en: The police chief told me, well, in that situation, if you'd called the police, we'd have arrested you because you were the only one who employed the use of deadly force.
sentences.zh: 警察局长告诉我，在那情况下，如果你报了警，我们反而会逮捕你，因为你是唯一一个使用致命武力的人。

sentences.en: And that made me angry because a 2,000-pound car and six drunk men and they would have arrested me.
sentences.zh: 这让我很生气，因为一辆2000磅重的车和六个醉汉，他们竟然要逮捕我。

sentences.en: It sounds like lawmakers in Florida were sympathetic to her argument.
sentences.zh: 听起来佛罗里达州的议员们很同情她的观点。

sentences.en: Well, not only have they been sympathetic to her argument,
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们不仅同情她的观点，

sentences.en: she has been able to mobilize voters on this issue to vote for and against candidates and to speak out for and against legislation throughout the years.
sentences.zh: 多年来，她还能够就这个问题动员选民去支持或反对候选人，并为立法大声疾呼。

sentences.en: That's probably where the NRA has been most effective.
sentences.zh: 这可能就是NRA最有效的地方。

sentences.en: And there was a huge political shift in Tallahassee.
sentences.zh: 塔拉哈西发生了一次巨大的政治转变。

sentences.en: The state capitol used to be run by Democrats for decades.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，州议会一直由民主党人掌控。

sentences.en: And then in the early 90s, that switched.
sentences.zh: 然后在90年代初，情况发生了变化。

sentences.en: This really is unusual because it looks like we're going to see a Republican sweep in Florida.
sentences.zh: 这确实很不寻常，因为看起来我们要在佛罗里达看到共和党的大获全胜。

sentences.en: To the point that by 1998.
sentences.zh: 以至于到了1998年。

sentences.en: A complete takeover of the state capitol.
sentences.zh: 完全接管了州议会。

sentences.en: Republicans held control of both the House and Senate.
sentences.zh: 共和党人控制了众议院和参议院。

sentences.en: And the governor's mansion with George Bush's son, Jeb Bush.
sentences.zh: 还有乔治·布什的儿子杰布·布什担任州长。

sentences.en: And they have in the 20 years since.
sentences.zh: 此后的20年里，他们一直保持着控制。

sentences.en: So the combination of someone powerful like Marion Hammer with the NRA and the Republican takeover in Tallahassee makes Florida a perfect environment for the NRA and the GOP to come together and push a pro-gun agenda.
sentences.zh: 所以，像玛丽恩·哈默这样有影响力的人物与NRA的结合，加上共和党在塔拉哈西的掌权，使佛罗里达成为NRA和共和党联手推动亲枪议程的完美环境。

sentences.en: This is a sensible law that other states have adopted because you shouldn't have to choose between being attacked or going to jail.
sentences.zh: 这是一项合理的法律，其他州也已经采纳，因为你不应该在遭受攻击或入狱之间做出选择。

sentences.en: We had Governor Jeb Bush who signed Stand Your Ground into law in 2005.
sentences.zh: 我们有杰布·布什州长，他在2005年签署了“不退让法”。

sentences.en: This is the law that means you have no duty to retreat if you feel threatened by deadly force.
sentences.zh: 这项法律意味着，如果你感到受到致命武力的威胁，你没有义务撤退。

sentences.en: You can use it.
sentences.zh: 你可以使用武力。

sentences.en: Popping up around Florida could be parking lots that double as arsenals.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达各地可能涌现出兼作军火库的停车场。

sentences.en: You had Governor Charlie CriSt.
sentences.zh: 当时有查理·克里斯特州长。

sentences.en: Governor Charlie Crist just signed a law that would allow people to keep a gun locked inside their cars outside of stores and businesses.
sentences.zh: 查理·克里斯特州长刚刚签署了一项法律，允许人们将枪支锁在商店和企业外的车内。

sentences.en: And now Governor Rick Scott, who has signed many laws in favor of gun owners in his eight-year term.
sentences.zh: 现在是里克·斯科特州长，他在八年任期内签署了许多有利于枪支拥有者的法律。

sentences.en: Governor Rick Scott has now signed more pro-gun bills into law in one term than any other governor in Florida history.
sentences.zh: 里克·斯科特州长现在签署的亲枪法案数量，比佛罗里达历史上任何一位州长在一个任期内签署的都要多。

sentences.en: For example, in 2011, it passed a bill known in Florida as Docs and Glocks.
sentences.zh: 例如，2011年，通过了一项在佛罗里达被称为“医生与格洛克”的法案。

sentences.en: This was a bill that prohibited doctors from asking patients if they had a gun at home.
sentences.zh: 这是一项禁止医生询问病人家里是否有枪的法案。

sentences.en: This is a question that pediatricians ask to make sure that guns are kept safely away from children.
sentences.zh: 这是儿科医生为了确保枪支远离儿童而询问的问题。

sentences.en: And Florida banned that, which doctors just kept saying was not okay because they needed to ask that for patients' own safety.
sentences.zh: 但佛罗里达禁止了这一点，医生们一直说这不对，因为他们需要为了病人的安全进行询问。

sentences.en: And in each of these cases, you've had Marion Hammer, who continues to head the NRA in Florida, be involved in pushing the legislation forward.
sentences.zh: 在每一个案例中，你都能看到继续领导佛罗里达州NRA的玛丽恩·哈默参与推动立法。

sentences.en: So Florida is a place where the NRA and gun rights advocates have a lot of sway and feel like they can experiment with the law and really push the envelope.
sentences.zh: 所以佛罗里达是一个NRA和枪支权利倡导者拥有很大影响力的地方，他们觉得可以尝试法律并真正挑战底线。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think people might be surprised that Florida has sort of been the first place to adopt some of these laws.
sentences.zh: 我想人们可能会惊讶，佛罗里达竟然是首批采纳其中一些法律的地方。

sentences.en: And so, over the past decade, you had several high-profile gun incidents in Florida.
sentences.zh: 因此，在过去十年里，佛罗里达发生了几起备受瞩目的枪支事件。

sentences.zh: 所以他们打算把所有枪支的购买年龄提高到21岁。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: They're going to extend a three-day waiting period also for all gun purchases, not just for handguns.
sentences.zh: 他们还将把所有枪支购买的三天等待期延长，不仅仅针对手枪。

sentences.en: Senators and guests in the gallery will please rise for the opening prayer to be given this morning.
sentences.zh: 请参议员和看台上的嘉宾起立，进行今早的开幕祈祷。

sentences.en: And they're going to put $400 million towards school safety and mental health prograMs.
sentences.zh: 他们还将投入4亿美元用于学校安全和心理健康项目。

sentences.en: So putting an armed police officer in every school, and at least one in every big high school,
sentences.zh: 即在每所学校配备一名武装警察，每所大型高中至少配备一名，

sentences.en: funding dedicated mental health counselors who are not also going to be teaching math.
sentences.zh: 资助专门的心理健康咨询师，他们不会同时担任数学老师。

sentences.en: Senator Galvano, having closed on Senate Bill 7026.
sentences.zh: 加尔瓦诺参议员，已结束对参议院第7026号法案的辩论。

sentences.en: And giving police more power to confiscate the weapons of people that they deemed troubled, even if only temporarily, so that they can't harm themselves or others.
sentences.zh: 并赋予警察更大的权力，没收他们认为有问题的个人的武器，即使只是暂时的，以防止他们伤害自己或他人。

sentences.en: And then, perhaps most controversially, putting more guns in schools in the hands of staff and some teachers.
sentences.zh: 然后，也许最具争议的是，让学校教职员工和部分教师携带更多枪支。

sentences.en: The secretary will unlock the board, and senators will prepare to vote, have all senators voted, lock the board and announce the vote.
sentences.zh: 秘书将解锁投票板，参议员们准备投票，所有参议员都投了吗？锁定投票板并宣布结果。

sentences.en: 20 a's, 18 nays, Mr. President.
sentences.zh: 20票赞成，18票反对，议长先生。

sentences.en: So the bill passes in the Senate by one vote.
sentences.zh: 所以该法案在参议院以一票之差通过了。

sentences.en: With that, we will stand in informal recess until promptly at 6.30 p.m.
sentences.zh: 至此，我们将休会，下午6点30分准时复会。

sentences.en: And the House will come to order.
sentences.zh: 众议院现在开会。

sentences.en: Members, please take your seats.
sentences.zh: 各位议员，请就座。

sentences.en: Then comes the real test, which is the House.
sentences.zh: 接下来是真正的考验，也就是众议院。

sentences.en: Which is a lot more conservative, and has more members who come from districts where gun control is not something you can run re-election on.
sentences.zh: 众议院要保守得多，而且有更多议员来自枪支管制不是竞选连任筹码的选区。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Perhaps something that can cost you re-election.
sentences.zh: 也许这会让你付出竞选连任的代价。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 正确。

sentences.en: Thank you, Mr. Speaker.
sentences.zh: 谢谢议长先生。

sentences.en: This is the Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School Public Safety Act.
sentences.zh: 这就是《玛乔丽·斯通曼·道格拉斯高中公共安全法案》。
zh_words: 玛乔丽·斯通曼·道格拉斯

sentences.en: So they start debating, and they go on for eight hours.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始辩论，持续了八个小时。

sentences.en: Representative Jenny, in debate.
sentences.zh: 詹妮众议员，请发言。

sentences.en: Thank you, Mr. Speaker.
sentences.zh: 谢谢议长先生。

sentences.en: You have Republican leaders, in what would have been unthinkable, just weeks earlier in the session, arguing for some gun control.
sentences.zh: 共和党领袖们在会议开始几周前还觉得不可思议的事情，现在却在为某些枪支管制措施进行辩论。

sentences.en: I do rise in support of this bill today.
sentences.zh: 我今天起身支持这项法案。

sentences.en: Let's prove to them that we can get it right this time.
sentences.zh: 让我们向他们证明，这一次我们能做对。

sentences.en: I'm going to vote up on this bill today because it's the right thing to do, and I hope you do too.
sentences.zh: 我今天会投票支持这项法案，因为这是正确的事，我希望你们也一样。

sentences.en: You have Democrats who say the bill is not everything we want, not even close.
sentences.zh: 民主党人则表示，这项法案并非我们想要的一切，甚至相去甚远。

sentences.en: But, you know, some of us are willing to vote with Republicans on this.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我们中有些人愿意就此与共和党人达成一致。

sentences.en: But make sure that whatever you vote, that you do it with a clear conscience, and that you're able to sleep when you go to bed at night.
sentences.zh: 但请确保无论你投什么票，都要问心无愧，晚上睡觉时能安然入眠。

sentences.en: Do not let our disagreements divide us.
sentences.zh: 不要让我们的分歧分裂我们。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: And then you have a group of Republican lawmakers who are not saying much at all.
sentences.zh: 还有一群共和党议员几乎什么都没说。

sentences.en: And these are Republicans from conservative or rural districts or who are running for statewide office in November in contested Republican primaries who oppose the bill.
sentences.zh: 这些共和党人来自保守派或农村选区，或者是在十一月共和党初选中竞选全州公职的人，他们反对这项法案。

sentences.en: And everybody knows that they oppose them.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道他们反对。

sentences.en: But they're not making stride in arguments in general because it's so fraught with emotion.
sentences.zh: 但他们并没有提出什么有力的论据，因为这件事充满了情感色彩。

sentences.en: You have the parents of the dead there.
sentences.zh: 死者的父母就在那里。

sentences.en: It's difficult to stand up and say, let's not do anything on guns.
sentences.zh: 站出来说“我们不要在枪支问题上做任何事”是很困难的。

sentences.en: So at this point, it looks like the bill is going to pass.
sentences.zh: 所以目前看来，这项法案很有可能会通过。

sentences.en: The key came when you realize that there were Democrats from Broward County who were going to vote yes.
sentences.zh: 关键在于你意识到布劳沃德县的民主党人也要投赞成票。

sentences.en: And not only were they going to vote yes, they were going to make the most persuasive argument for other Democrats to join them.
sentences.zh: 而且他们不仅要投赞成票，还要为其他民主党人加入他们提供最有说服力的论据。

sentences.en: And the culmination of this is the final speech.
sentences.zh: 而这一切的高潮就是最后的演讲。

sentences.en: Representative Moskowitz, you're recognized.
sentences.zh: 莫斯科维茨众议员，请发言。

sentences.en: By Representative Jared Moskowitz of Coral Springs, which is right next door to Parkland.
sentences.zh: 由来自科勒尔斯普林斯的贾里德·莫斯科维茨众议员发言，那里就在帕克兰隔壁。

sentences.en: Thank you, Mr. Speaker.
sentences.zh: 谢谢议长先生。

sentences.en: He is a Stoneman Douglas graduate.
sentences.zh: 他是斯通曼·道格拉斯高中的毕业生。

sentences.en: People, when I would tell them, hey, I'm an elected official.
sentences.zh: 人们，当我告诉他们，嘿，我是民选官员。

sentences.en: I'm on this commission from the city of Parkland.
sentences.zh: 我是帕克兰市委员会的成员。

sentences.en: The first thing they would say to me is, where the hell is Parkland?
sentences.zh: 他们对我说的第一句话就是，帕克兰到底在哪儿？

sentences.en: Well, now the world knows where Parkland is.
sentences.zh: 好吧，现在全世界都知道帕克兰在哪儿了。

sentences.en: And his four-year-old son was in preschool down the street from the shooting.
sentences.zh: 他四岁的儿子当时就在离枪击案现场几条街外的幼儿园里。

sentences.en: He had been so happy, had to learn to write his name, but he wanted to get better.
sentences.zh: 他一直很开心，刚学会写自己的名字，但他想写得更好。

sentences.en: So we signed him up for a writing class.
sentences.zh: 所以我们给他报了一个写作班。

sentences.en: That writing class was going on in Parkland on the afternoon of February 14th, around the corner from Douglas.
sentences.zh: 那个写作班在2月14日下午就在帕克兰进行，就在道格拉斯高中拐角处。

sentences.en: And?
sentences.zh: 然后呢？

sentences.en: And that class was taught by Jen Guttenberg.
sentences.zh: 那个班是由詹·古滕伯格教的。

sentences.en: The boy's teacher had her daughter at Stoneman Douglas.
sentences.zh: 那个男孩的老师把她的女儿送到了斯通曼·道格拉斯高中。

sentences.en: You see, she lost her daughter, Jamie, while she was teaching my son how to write.
sentences.zh: 你看，她在教我儿子写字的时候，失去了她的女儿杰米。

sentences.en: She put my kid in a closet when her daughter died.
sentences.zh: 当她的女儿去世时，她把我的孩子关进了壁橱里。

sentences.en: I wanted to say thank you at the funeral.
sentences.zh: 我在葬礼上想说声谢谢。

sentences.en: I didn't know how to do that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道该怎么做。

sentences.en: I hope that when I push the green button, that will show all the appreciation that I need and that she needs.
sentences.zh: 我希望当我按下绿色按钮时，那能表达出我所需要表达的，以及她所需要的全部感激之情。

sentences.en: You don't need to stand with me.
sentences.zh: 你们不需要支持我。

sentences.en: I don't need you to stand with me.
sentences.zh: 我不需要你们支持我。

sentences.en: I need you to stand with the families.
sentences.zh: 我需要你们支持那些家庭。

sentences.en: Push the green button.
sentences.zh: 按下绿色按钮。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: So if there were people still on the fence by that point, this was the speech that probably would have pushed them to voting yes.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果当时还有人犹豫不决，这番演讲很可能促使他们投下赞成票。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I have never seen the House chamber so rapt at a speech from someone in the back of the room because the Democrats sit in the back, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我从未见过众议院会议厅对坐在后排的人的演讲如此专注，因为民主党人坐在后排，你知道的，

sentences.en: and they don't have any power in Tallahassee.
sentences.zh: 他们在塔拉哈西没有任何权力。

sentences.en: But they listen to every word of that speech.
sentences.zh: 但他们听了那场演讲的每一个字。

sentences.en: So after this speech, then what happens?
sentences.zh: 那么在这场演讲之后，发生了什么？

sentences.en: The clerk will unlock the machine and the members will proceed to vote.
sentences.zh: 书记员将解锁机器，议员们将进行投票。

sentences.en: They call the vote in the House and they open the board for people to vote yes or no.
sentences.zh: 他们在众议院宣布投票，并打开投票板供人们投赞成或反对票。

sentences.en: All members voted.
sentences.zh: 所有议员都已投票。

sentences.en: And the votes go on the board.
sentences.zh: 投票结果显示在板上。

sentences.en: Clerk will lock the machine and announce the vote.
sentences.zh: 书记员将锁定机器并宣布投票结果。

sentences.en: 67 yeas.
sentences.zh: 67票赞成。

sentences.en: 15 nays, Mr. Speaker.
sentences.zh: 15票反对，议长先生。

sentences.en: And the bill passes.
sentences.zh: 法案通过了。

sentences.en: Show the bill passes.
sentences.zh: 显示法案通过。

sentences.en: Read the next bill.
sentences.zh: 宣读下一项法案。

sentences.en: I want to thank everyone for being here today.
sentences.zh: 我想感谢今天到场的每一个人。

sentences.en: I cannot possibly convey to you the grief that I have seen and felt in attending funerals and spending time with these families.
sentences.zh: 我无法向你们表达我在参加葬礼和陪伴这些家庭时所见所感的悲痛。

sentences.en: And then the final hurdle is what will Governor Rick Scott do?
sentences.zh: 最后的障碍是里克·斯科特州长会怎么做？

sentences.en: Because this was not exactly the legislation that he had championed.
sentences.zh: 因为这并不是他所倡导的立法。

sentences.en: There were some differences.
sentences.zh: 其中存在一些分歧。

sentences.en: And he is expected to run for the United States Senate in Florida later this year, challenge the Democrat, Bill Nelson.
sentences.zh: 预计他今年晚些时候将竞选佛罗里达州的联邦参议员，挑战民主党人比尔·尼尔森。

sentences.en: And he has had the support of the NRA in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 而且他过去一直得到全国步枪协会（NRA）的支持。

sentences.en: So he could have decided to veto the bill.
sentences.zh: 所以他本可以决定否决这项法案。

sentences.en: But he asks the families from Parkland of the victims to come to Tallahassee and he meets with them.
sentences.zh: 但他要求帕克兰的受害者家属来到塔拉哈西，并与他们会面。

sentences.en: And they tell him they don't like everything in the law, but they would like him to sign it.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉他，他们并不喜欢法律中的所有内容，但他们希望他签署。

sentences.en: And he comes out and he tells the press with the family standing behind him.
sentences.zh: 他走出来，在家人站在他身后时告诉媒体。

sentences.en: There are things of this bill that I oppose.
sentences.zh: 这项法案中有些内容我反对。

sentences.en: And I've been pretty open about that.
sentences.zh: 对此我一直很坦诚。

sentences.en: That he doesn't like everything in the law.
sentences.zh: 他并不喜欢法律中的所有内容。

sentences.en: So after reviewing the entire bill, I had to ask myself.
sentences.zh: 所以在审阅了整个法案后，我不得不问自己。

sentences.en: Will this bill make a huge investment and dramatically improve school safety?
sentences.zh: 这项法案会进行巨额投资并显著改善学校安全吗？

sentences.en: In hopes of never seeing another tragedy like this again.
sentences.zh: 希望能永远不再看到这样的悲剧。

sentences.en: Will this bill provide more funding to treat the mentally ill?
sentences.zh: 这项法案会提供更多资金来治疗精神疾病患者吗？

sentences.en: Will this bill give far more tools to keep guns away from people who should not have them?
sentences.zh: 这项法案会提供更多工具来防止不该拥有枪支的人获得枪支吗？

sentences.en: The answer to all three is yes.
sentences.zh: 这三个问题的答案都是肯定的。

sentences.en: And that is why I'm signing the legislation today.
sentences.zh: 这就是我今天签署这项立法的原因。

sentences.en: And so for the first time in 20 years of Republican control, Florida passed new gun restrictions in defiance of the NRA.
sentences.zh: 因此，在共和党控制佛罗里达州20年来，该州首次在无视全国步枪协会的情况下通过了新的枪支限制措施。

sentences.en: What had changed to bring these Republicans to a place to do something that they clearly would not have done in the past?
sentences.zh: 是什么改变了这些共和党人，让他们去做一些过去显然不会做的事情？

sentences.en: Well, there were several factors at play.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有几个因素在起作用。

sentences.en: Public opinion polls showed that a majority of Florida voters favor some sort of gun control.
sentences.zh: 民意调查显示，大多数佛罗里达州选民支持某种形式的枪支管制。

sentences.en: And so maybe that pushed some Republicans into a position where they were willing to compromise.
sentences.zh: 所以也许这促使一些共和党人处于愿意妥协的位置。

sentences.en: You had Democratic lawmakers agreeing to work with Republicans, even if they didn't like everything that was in the bill, just to say, we have to pass something.
sentences.zh: 民主党议员同意与共和党人合作，即使他们不喜欢法案中的所有内容，只是为了说，我们必须通过一些东西。

sentences.en: Something is better than nothing.
sentences.zh: 有总比没有好。

sentences.en: The timing was important because the legislature was still in session and had just enough time to get a bill drafted and passed.
sentences.zh: 时机很重要，因为立法机构仍在开会，刚好有足够的时间起草并通过法案。

sentences.en: And then, of course, there were the students.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有学生们。

sentences.en: The students were so vocal and active on social media, on mainstream media, and just showing up in person to the state capitol.
sentences.zh: 学生们在社交媒体、主流媒体上非常直言不讳和活跃，并亲自出现在州议会大厦。

sentences.en: And they were impossible to ignore.
sentences.zh: 他们让人无法忽视。

sentences.en: And then there was a trip that lawmakers took from both chambers of the legislature that went to Stoneman Douglas High School in the two days immediately following the shooting when it was still closed off by police tape.
sentences.zh: 此外，立法机构两院的议员们在枪击案发生后的两天内，在警察封锁现场的情况下，前往了斯通曼·道格拉斯高中。

sentences.en: And they walked the hallways and they saw the deep red bloodstains in the halls and the bullet pocked walls and the backpacks and stuff laying everywhere.
sentences.zh: 他们走过走廊，看到了大厅里深红色的血迹、布满弹孔的墙壁，以及到处散落的书包等物品。

sentences.en: The police officers showed them where the gunmen tried to shoot out at people running from the building.
sentences.zh: 警察向他们展示了枪手试图射击从大楼里逃出来的人的地方。

sentences.en: And the police told them only because there's hurricane impact glass was this tragedy not worse than it already was.
sentences.zh: 警察告诉他们，如果不是因为有防飓风玻璃，这场悲剧会比现在更糟糕。

sentences.en: They picked up scraps of paper that kids had, you know, left behind.
sentences.zh: 他们捡起了孩子们留下的纸片。

sentences.en: And some of them were from, you know, social studies class, AP government class, where they were studying how a bill becomes a law.
sentences.zh: 其中一些来自社会研究课、AP政府课，他们在那里学习法案是如何成为法律的。

sentences.en: And I think that personal connection just underscored for them how important this was.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种个人联系对他们来说，强调了这件事的重要性。

sentences.en: The Senate sponsor, Bill Galvana, who's the incoming Senate president, told me going to Stoneman Douglas was like going to a graveyard.
sentences.zh: 参议院发起人比尔·加尔瓦诺，即将上任的参议院议长，告诉我，去斯通曼·道格拉斯就像去墓地一样。

sentences.en: I'm reminded of the story that you told at the beginning of our conversation about Marion Hammer, the lobbyist from the NRA,
sentences.zh: 我想起了你在我们谈话开始时讲的关于全国步枪协会说客玛丽恩·哈默的故事，

sentences.en: who was able to communicate her own very personal and traumatic experience with guns to push for gun rights.
sentences.zh: 她能够传达自己非常个人化和创伤性的枪支经历，以推动枪支权利。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's the personal anecdote that helped get the gun laws passed for years in Florida to make them less restrictive.
sentences.zh: 是的，正是这些个人轶事帮助佛罗里达州多年来通过了枪支法律，使其限制减少。

sentences.en: And now it's the anecdotes of lawmakers and meeting with students who were victims in Parkland, getting them to to restrict them again.
sentences.zh: 而现在，是议员们的轶事以及与作为帕克兰受害者的学生会面，让他们再次限制枪支。

sentences.en: But we should remember the many other anecdotes that did not get action because they were not taking place at this particular moment where the emotions were so raw,
sentences.zh: 但我们应该记住，许多其他轶事并没有得到行动，因为它们没有发生在此时此刻，当时情绪如此强烈，

sentences.en: where the politics were in place for the legislature to change.
sentences.zh: 当时政治环境也适合立法机构做出改变。

sentences.en: So Florida, this state that's been so friendly to guns in a matter of just weeks, does something that has been almost unthinkable on the national stage.
sentences.zh: 所以佛罗里达州，这个对枪支如此友好的州，在短短几周内就做出了在全国舞台上几乎不可思议的事情。

sentences.en: Is this indicative of perhaps how the issue of guns might play out across the country and maybe in the congressional midterm elections coming up this fall?
sentences.zh: 这是否预示着枪支问题可能会在全国范围内，以及今年秋季即将到来的国会中期选举中如何发展？

sentences.en: Or is it because of the special circumstances and the power of the personal anecdote that somehow might make this unreplicable and maybe impossible to repeat elsewhere?
sentences.zh: 还是因为特殊情况和个人轶事的力量，使得这在其他地方可能无法复制，甚至不可能重复？

sentences.en: I don't think we know yet.
sentences.zh: 我想我们还不知道。

sentences.en: The students are going to try to replicate this elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 学生们将尝试在其他地方复制这一点。

sentences.en: I think they might find it difficult to do outside of Florida.

sentences.en: On Wednesday, the Prime Minister of Britain, Theresa May,
sentences.zh: 周三，英国首相特蕾莎·梅，

sentences.en: ordered the immediate expulsion of 23 Russian diplomats as punishment for using a chemical weapon on British soil to poison a former Russian spy.
sentences.zh: 下令立即驱逐23名俄罗斯外交官，作为对在英国领土上使用化学武器毒害一名前俄罗斯间谍的惩罚。

sentences.en: This will be the single biggest expulsion for over 30 years.
sentences.zh: 这将是30多年来最大规模的一次驱逐行动。

sentences.en: May has accused Russia of using a rare nerve agent to try to kill Sergei Skripal, a double agent who sold Russian secrets to Britain.

sentences.en: He remains in critical condition.
sentences.zh: 他目前仍处于危急状态。

sentences.en: In a statement, Russia called the expulsions, quote, totally unacceptable, unjustified, and short-sighted.
sentences.zh: 在一份声明中，俄罗斯称这些驱逐行动是“完全不可接受、毫无根据且短视的”。

sentences.en: And the Times reports that with a 627-vote lead, the Democratic candidate for Congress in Pennsylvania, Conor Lamb,
